Specifically, Hydrocortisone is linked to Musculoskeletal System Disease and Exfoliative Dermatitis, both of which are associated with Triamcinolone, a corticosteroid with similar pharmacological effects. Triamcinolone, in turn, is linked to Autoimmune Disease, indicating a potential mechanistic pathway involving corticosteroid-induced immunosuppression. The low final scores in the paths suggest that while there is a clinical association, the evidence is not robust enough to definitively establish a causal relationship. The integration of these paths highlights the role of corticosteroids in modulating immune responses, but further research is needed to confirm the exact mechanism and clinical relevance.
